samples: This module reads and validates a service configuration from a JSON file, ensuring that port numbers fall within valid TCP ranges and worker counts stay between 1 and 64. It provides functions to load the configuration with error reporting, use sensible defaults when the file is missing or invalid, or fall back to a caller-supplied configuration. The module is useful for any service that needs to start up with validated settings from an external file.

This module reads and validates a service configuration from a JSON file, ensuring that port numbers fall within valid TCP ranges and worker counts stay between 1 and 64. It provides functions to load the configuration with error reporting, use sensible defaults when the file is missing or invalid, or fall back to a caller-provided configuration. The module defines the configuration structure and the possible errors that can occur during loading.

This module reads and validates a service configuration from a JSON file, ensuring that port numbers fall within valid TCP ranges and worker counts stay between 1 and 64. It provides functions to load the configuration with error reporting, use sensible defaults when the file is missing or invalid, or fall back to a caller-supplied configuration. The module defines the configuration structure with three settings (port, number of workers, and logging verbosity) and detailed error types to help diagnose loading failures.

This module loads and validates a service configuration from a JSON file, ensuring that the port number is valid (1–65535), the worker count is between 1 and 64, and the log level is one of three predefined options. It provides multiple ways to load the configuration: directly from a file with detailed error reporting, with automatic fallback to sensible defaults, or with a custom fallback configuration. The module is designed to be the single source of truth for how a service initializes its runtime settings.
